title: Spread of Entanglement in Generalized Kicked Ising Chain
authors: Tanay Pathak, Hiromi Ebisu, Tomaž Prosen
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of entanglement in a generalized version of the kicked Ising chain, extending the model from the standard qubit case (local dimension $q=2$) to higher local dimensions ($q > 2$). We identify the existence of ''dual-unitary'' points where the model's space-time duality allows for exact analytical solutions. Our analysis reveals that while a few unique dual-unitary points exist analytically for systems with local dimensions $q=3$ and $q=4$, such points do not exist for $q \ge 5$ due to the lack of a unique kicking strength that satisfies the required matrix element conditions. Utilizing the transfer matrix method and a replica trick specifically adapted for higher dimensions, we derive exact expressions for the growth of entanglement entropy in the $q=3$ (kicked Potts-type) model starting from a class of solvable initial states. Our results demonstrate that at the dual-unitary point, both Rényi and von Neumann entanglement entropies grow linearly with time until reaching a maximum value determined by the subsystem size.
summary: This paper analyzes the dynamics of entanglement spread in an extended kicked Ising chain model, generalizing it from qubits to higher local dimensions. The core finding is that exact analytical solutions (dual-unitary points) are restricted to low dimensions ($q \le 4$). For solvable cases, the theory predicts linear growth of entanglement entropy until saturation at these special points.
main_problem: The study investigates how entanglement spreads over time in a generalized kicked Ising chain, extending the model beyond standard qubits to higher local dimensions.
main_result: Dual-unitary points, which allow for exact analytical solutions, only exist for local dimensions $q \le 4$, failing for $q \ge 5$ due to constraints on matrix elements. For solvable cases like $q=3$, entanglement entropy grows linearly with time at the dual-unitary point.
method: The analysis employs the transfer matrix method and a replica trick adapted for higher dimensions, alongside deriving specific conditions (Equation 30) that must be met for duality.
model_or_system: The system is the Generalized Kicked Ising Chain (KIM), which models quantum dynamics under periodic driving. It generalizes from qubits ($q=2$) to systems with local dimension $q>2$, corresponding to kicked Potts-type models for $q=3$.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy (Rényi and von Neumann); the existence of 'dual-unitary' points.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that specific matrix element conditions must hold for dual-unitarity, which leads to contradictions for $q \ge 5$. For large $q$, summation is approximated by integration.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; mentions Table I showing calculated values of $b$ for small $q$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the generalized model and identifying the dual-unitarity condition via matrix elements, to proving its existence/non-existence based on $q$, and finally deriving exact expressions for entanglement growth in solvable cases.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding quantum chaos and thermalization dynamics in extended lattice models by linking spectral properties (dual-unitarity) to entanglement scaling laws.
